q: The Kolmogorov complexity K(x) of a string x is defined as the length of the shortest program for a universal Turing machine that outputs x. K(x) is:
opts: Upper semi-computable (can be approximated from above)
Lower semi-computable (can be approximated from below)
exp: K(x) is upper semi-computable: we can enumerate all programs and their outputs, so K(x) ≤ some d we discover. But K(x) is not computable—the minimal-length program cannot be found in general.
